result.title: Auditing World-Model Explanations in Retail Forecasting: Faithfulness, Accuracy and Price Response
result.summary: Forecasting models that read the price and promotion plan explain each forecast as a baseline, what would sell with nothing planned, plus the lift the plan adds. We test such explanations with eight checks, six with a pass rule fixed before any result, and find that passing them does not make an explanation right. In generated store data with known effects, a world model passes the checks of construction, stability, price direction and agreement with sales and with LightGBM, yet its lifts are 1.33 to 1.40 times the truth when merchants plan into high-demand weeks, and 1.23 to 1.42 times in eight variants of that world. It still picks the right weeks to promote, but stock ordered to its lift is off by 0.44 to 0.48 of the true lift. Its stated response to a lasting regular-price change is 4.7 to 6.5 times the true -0.5, and only a measured cause finds this. On Dominick's, 38 episodes in which a store's regular prices sat apart from its zone peers give a noisy benchmark: a pooled 8-week response of -0.33 (95% interval -0.68 to 0.01). For the final tuned world models of our companion paper on nine data sets, baseline and lift add up under each model's own plan, but a deeper price cut lowers the forecast in 29% to 83% of item-week steps on Dominick's (23% to 80% within prices seen in training), and the world model and LightGBM both state about twice the measured response. Across 703 configurations from the settings searches, checks passed were not related to forecast accuracy (Spearman 0.02, 95% interval -0.02 to 0.05); with no known answer for those versions, this concerns accuracy, while whether an explanation is right is measured only in the generated data.

AI.brief_summary: 论文为零售预测类「世界模型」的基线+增量式解释设置八项事前检查（构造、稳定性、价格方向、与销量和 LightGBM 的一致性等），并在已知真值的合成数据与 Dominick's 数据上检验这些检查通过是否意味着解释正确。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽与视觉推理无关，但其「检查全过仍不忠实、唯有实测因果效应才能暴露偏差」的审计框架可能供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态是否真正使用视觉证据、以及如何设计忠实性评价。
